result.summary: Enables SQLite's `secure_delete` PRAGMA by default on all wallet database connections and sets `-DSQLITE_SECURE_DELETE` in the SQLite depends package. Deleted or updated database records are overwritten with zeroes instead of remaining in unallocated SQLite database pages. Removes the `WalletDatabase::Rewrite` interface (which previously invoked `VACUUM` only upon initial encryption) and adds functional tests for plaintext and rotated key erasure.
result.problem: Modifications and deletions in SQLite wallet files leave data in unallocated database pages. Initial encryption previously avoided leaving unencrypted keys in slack space by running an explicit `VACUUM` rewrite, but other sensitive operations—such as rotating master encryption keys during passphrase changes—left obsolete key records visible in database free space.
evidence: PR description: 'l0rinc's LLMs recently found changing the passphrase can leave the original that encryption key record in free pages. We should want to ensure that those records are also deleted... Note that this behavior appears to be present since wallet encryption was initially introduced in #352.'

PR description: 'Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch, and NixOS all set SQLite's compile time option to default secure_delete to enabled... This suggests to me that the performance penalty is not actually that bad.'
result.card: Enables SQLite's secure_delete PRAGMA by default for wallet databases and enables the compile-time flag in depends builds, zeroing out deleted or updated records on disk. Overwriting or deleting records previously left residual data in SQLite free space unless an explicit database rewrite (VACUUM) was run, meaning rotated master keys remained unpurged after passphrase changes. The change removes the now-redundant WalletDatabase::Rewrite method and adds functional tests ensuring unencrypted private keys and rotated master keys do not remain in the database file.

risk.why: A flaw in SQLite PRAGMA configuration or database page handling could corrupt wallet databases or leave plaintext private keys unpurged on disk.
